title: An Octopus Has Three Hearts
script: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood. Two hearts push blood through its gills. The third sends it to the rest of the body. Its blood uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen, and that makes it blue. Here's the strange part. When an octopus swims, its main heart stops beating. That's why it would rather crawl than swim. So an animal with three hearts gets tired easily.
description: An octopus has three hearts, blue blood, and a main heart that stops when it swims.

title: Venus Spins Slower Than It Orbits
script: Venus spins so slowly that one rotation takes longer than its entire year. A single spin takes about 243 Earth days. Its trip around the Sun takes only about 225. It also spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west. Sunrise to sunrise takes about 117 Earth days. On Venus, a year ends before the planet finishes even one spin.
description: Venus rotates once every 243 Earth days, but orbits the Sun in about 225.

title: Lightning Is Hotter Than the Sun's Surface
script: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun. The Sun's surface is around 5,500 degrees Celsius. Lightning can reach roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius, about five times hotter. It heats the air so fast that the air explodes outward. That sudden expansion is the sound we call thunder. So thunder is really the sound of air being blasted apart.
description: Lightning heats the air to about five times the temperature of the Sun's surface.

title: Your Brain Burns 20 Percent of Your Energy
script: Your brain is only about two percent of your body weight. But it burns around twenty percent of your energy. That's true even while you rest. Billions of neurons keep sending signals, and that takes a lot of fuel. Hard thinking adds only a small extra amount. So the small organ in your head is the biggest energy user you own.
description: The brain makes up about 2 percent of body weight but uses about 20 percent of its energy.

title: A Million Earths Fit Inside the Sun
script: More than a million Earths could fit inside the Sun. The Sun holds about 99.8 percent of all the mass in our solar system. Every planet, moon and asteroid shares the tiny amount left over. Jupiter alone makes up most of that. Yet the Sun is only an average-sized star. So our giant Sun is really just a small star in a huge galaxy.
description: The Sun is so large that over a million Earths could fit inside it.

title: Oxford Is Older Than the Aztec Empire
script: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire. Teaching was already happening at Oxford by the year 1096. The Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325. That means students were studying in England about two hundred years before the Aztecs built their city. History doesn't line up neatly by continent. Some universities are older than entire empires.
description: Teaching at Oxford began around 1096, long before the Aztec capital was founded in 1325.

title: The First Computer Bug Was a Real Moth
script: The first computer bug on record was a real moth. In 1947, operators of the Harvard Mark II found a moth stuck inside a relay. They taped it into the logbook and noted it was an actual bug. Engineers had used the word for glitches long before that. But this moth made the joke famous. Now every software glitch carries the name of one unlucky insect.
description: In 1947 operators found a moth in the Harvard Mark II and taped it into the logbook.
source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History (Mark II moth)

title: A Banana Is a Berry But a Strawberry Isn't
script: Botanically, a banana is a berry, but a strawberry is not. A true berry grows from a single flower ovary and has seeds inside the flesh. Bananas, grapes and tomatoes all fit that rule. A strawberry grows differently. Its tiny seeds sit on the outside, and each one is actually its own fruit. So the fruit called a berry isn't one, and the one that isn't, is.
description: By botanical definition a banana is a berry, while a strawberry is not.

title: Honey Almost Never Spoils
script: Honey barely spoils when it's stored properly. It contains very little water, so bacteria struggle to grow in it. It's also acidic, and bees add an enzyme that makes a little hydrogen peroxide. Together, these make honey a terrible home for microbes. Sealed honey can stay good for years. The sweetest food in your kitchen is also one of the hardest places for bacteria to live.
description: Low water, acidity and natural hydrogen peroxide keep honey from spoiling.

title: A Teaspoon of Neutron Star Weighs Billions of Tons
script: A teaspoon of neutron star would weigh billions of tons. When a giant star collapses, its core can be squeezed into a ball only about twenty kilometers wide. Yet that ball holds more mass than our Sun. Atoms are crushed so tightly that almost everything becomes neutrons. So an object the size of a city can outweigh an entire star.
description: Neutron stars pack more mass than the Sun into a ball about 20 kilometers wide.
